messages:
Mia Gonzalez: Hi team! Quick onboarding Qs after my first week. I completed the Workday packet but still have a few things unclear: 1) When will my health/dental/vision actually start? 2) I bought a keyboard ($89.99) for the home office — reimbursement route? 3) My offer mentioned pro-rated holidays and a 90-day rule for PTO — can someone clarify what I can take in month 1? 4) Is there any extra paperwork for adding a domestic partner to benefits? Thanks!

Lina Patel (People Ops): welcome Mia :wave: short answers up front: 1) Benefits effective date is usually the first of the month after 30 days from your start (e.g., start 06/10 -> effective 07/01). 2) Reimburse via Spendesk (https://tools.redwood/spendesk). Attach itemized receipt + proof of payment and tag your manager for approval. 3) PTO accrues from day 1 but many teams require 90 days before taking extended leave; managers can approve exceptions case-by-case. Company holidays are pro-rated during first year. 4) Domestic partner: yes, you'll upload a domestic partner affidavit during the benefits enrollment flow; also need SSN + DOB for dependents.

Mia Gonzalez: Thanks Lina. I started 2024-06-12 so coverage would be 07/01? Also, does 'first of the month after 30 days' ever get overridden if carrier processes quicker?

HR-bot: Enrollment reminder: benefits invite sent to mia.gonzalez@redwood.com on 2024-06-12. Vendor processing windows may vary; carrier decisions are final but exceptions for urgent care are handled via case review.

Lina Patel: Correct — expected 07/01 for a 06/12 start. Occasionally carriers will backdate in special circumstances but we don't guarantee that. DM me if you have a specific claim before 07/01 and we'll start a case.

Mia Gonzalez: Got it. For the keyboard receipt, is a photo of the card statement + store receipt enough? And is <$100 considered a small purchase or does it need pre-approval?

Oliver Grant (Manager): Hi Mia 44b photo + receipt is fine. Under $100 is usually fine to submit after purchase; anything $250+ needs pre-approval. Please tag me (oliver.grant) when you submit so I can approve quickly.

Mia Gonzalez: Awesome thanks. One more payroll nuance: my offer showed USD salary but I'm in CA and my bank is US — will my paychecks be on the usual biweekly Friday schedule? Also what's the payroll cutoff?

Lina Patel: Payroll is biweekly + direct deposit on Fridays. Cutoff is Tuesday 11:59pm PT for that Friday's run. If your forms were completed after cutoff, your first pay may land the next cycle; we may do a retro starter payment in the following run if needed. If you want confirmation, DM payroll@redwood with your start date and direct deposit confirmation and we'll confirm your expected first payday.

Mia Gonzalez: I uploaded direct deposit yesterday. Will do a DM to payroll. And about holidays: if I start mid-December, do I get paid for the company winter closure that year?

Tara Singh (People Ops): short version: company wide closures (winter break) are pro-rated for the first year. If your start date is before the closure date we'll pro-rate your entitlement; specifics depend on your hire month. If you have a specific start date, we can calc it for you.

Mia Gonzalez: Thanks Tara. Final question: is there any special form to get reimbursed for travel in a different currency (I had to fly into HQ and paid in GBP)?

Finance-bot: For foreign currency expenses: submit original receipt + proof of payment in Spendesk. Spendesk will record the FX conversion using the transaction date. If finance needs a manual conversion, we'll use the bank FX rate and note it in the reimbursement. Over policy thresholds (> $250 equiv) may need extra documentation.

Mia Gonzalez: Great, submitting Spendesk now and DMing payroll. Appreciate the help everyone! :smile:

Oliver Grant: Welcome again Mia 389 tag me if you need fast approval on Spendesk.

Lina Patel: Ping us if any of the links don't work or if the benefits invite got lost. We're happy to walk through the portal on a quick call.

Mia Gonzalez: Will do, thanks all!
